No mechanize keys leak onto audit output.

The guard tests assert the contract on raw JSON bytes, not on a decoded map: `"role_streaks": []` and `"spec_coverage_clean_rounds": null` are string-asserted, and `"role_streaks": null` is asserted absent, which is the discriminating check against the nil-slice defect class. --compact is proven to have taken effect via the absent harness_stale key rather than assumed. Streak entries are asserted to carry exactly 3 keys, so a new field cannot arrive unnoticed. go test ./... exits 0.

The agent-facing wording is pinned as verbatim substrings in README.md, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.md, and divergence.hint is asserted against engine.DivergenceHint rather than a literal copy, so the shipped constant, the docs and the test cannot drift apart. I re-read REFERENCE.md L490-656 against the emitted bytes: the documented shapes (always-[] arrays, always-emitted null key, omitted-not-null object, --compact survival, the three message forms) all match what the binary emits.

Both prompt-emission sites (panel and standalone regression) are asserted against the same expected list, and the empty-list case asserts the sentence is absent entirely rather than present-with-nothing-after-it. Registration order is pinned over three out-of-alphabetical entries, which is what distinguishes this list from the ascending mechanized_classes. The all-invalid case is proven via the stderr skip notices, since mechanical_checks is omitempty and cannot distinguish ran-and-returned-nothing from never-called.

The reviewer exclusion sentence now guards on engine.ReviewerExclusionClasses' emptiness rather than len(checks), so an all-invalid workflow appends no sentence instead of one ending in an empty list, while each entry's skip notice still fires. Class order is registration order (deterministic, not map iteration). reviewResult.MechanicalChecks carries omitempty (L101), so a nil slice omits the key rather than serializing null.

Ran the binary: mechanized_classes emits [] when nothing was withheld and mechanize_candidates emits [] when the filter removed every candidate — neither flips to null. Both survive --compact (verified with harness_stale absent as the proof --compact applied). The register-a-check hint is dropped when the candidate list empties, so the agent is never told to write a check that exists. Sorted ascending, each class once. The roleless-row advisory is one per file, honours --quiet, and goes to stderr so piped JSON stays parseable.

The exclusion sentence takes its own guard, separate from the checks-running guard, so an all-invalid workflow still runs its checks and emits its notices while appending no sentence. Same membership rule and same registration order as the panel site — one shared helper, so the two prompt sites cannot drift. mechChecks is nil when no check is registered, but MechanicalChecks carries omitempty, so the key is omitted rather than emitted as null.

filterMechanizedCandidates returns both halves from one split, so kept and withheld cannot disagree; both are make()'d non-nil, which is what keeps the two emitted arrays [] instead of null. It runs strictly after the frequency threshold, so suppressing one class never changes whether another crosses it. mechanizeClassesFromRounds now takes checks, making --status a real suppression sink for next_action rather than a projection. --report stays unfiltered by design (Non-Goal 9); README L550 and SKILL.md L239 both state that residual to the driver.

Verified: --status emits neither mechanize_candidates nor mechanized_classes (nothing for it to explain) yet honours suppression through next_action, which falls through to the run-the-next-round directive once every candidate is mechanized. Observation, not a defect and predating this release: mechanical_checks carries {class,cmd} on a bare --status and {class,cmd,passed,exit_code,+output_tail} under --check. The shape is self-describing (absent passed = not run) and REFERENCE L636 relies on the bare form, but the two shapes are nowhere spelled out for a parsing agent.

Both empty cases are covered by opposite fixtures and asserted against raw JSON, including the discriminating `": null"` absence assertions for mechanize_candidates and mechanized_classes. Ordering is pinned against a fixture where ascending differs from both registration order and the total-descending candidate order. --compact survival is proven with the absent harness_stale key. --report's unchanged behaviour is pinned so suppression cannot silently spread to it.
